column3: JCX-67-17, Estimated Budget Effects of the Conference Agreement for H.R.1, the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, row "B. 21 Percent Corporate Tax Rate" (outline position II.B; the statute is P.L. 115-97 sec. 13001)
column15: Printed in BILLIONS, not millions. Annual path -101.3/-125.3/-130.5/-131.1/-132.6/-136.2/-140.7/-144.7/-149.7/-156.3; five-year -620.8. The line is 92.6% of the bill's -1,456.0 NET TOTAL. JCT's table carries no section-number column, and JCT's stacking convention (Revenue Estimating Process, Jan 2025, slide 18) may put a rate change first, without the interaction, so this row is not an isolated rate score in the way the Options rows are. Note the near-collision with `biden_corporate_28`'s -1,347.0: two different reforms in opposite directions, 1.5 apart.

column3: JCX-42-21, Estimated Budgetary Effects of an Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute to the Revenue Provisions of Subtitles F-J ... scheduled for markup 14 September 2021, row "A. Increase in corporate tax rate to 26.5 percent"
column15: NOT comparable per point without the caveat. H.R. 5376 sec. 138101 replaces the flat 21% with 18% up to $400,000, 21% to $5,000,000 and 26.5% above, plus a recapture above $10,000,000 - so the bottom of the base is CUT 3pp while the top rises 5.5pp, and the row also bundles the dividends-received-deduction change with no separate line. Dividing by 5.5 therefore UNDERSTATES the marginal base of the top tranche. Annual path ($M) 39275/48712/50536/51760/53154/57314/59558/59926/59698/60161. The House-PASSED bill (JCX-45-21, JCX-46-21) contains no corporate rate change at all - it was replaced by CAMT and the buyback excise, not rescored.

column15: Conventional. Dynamic is -643.7 (Feb 2021) / -693.9 (Options 2.0), with GDP -0.7%, capital stock -1.4%, wages -0.6% and -138,000 FTE. THE ONE NON-GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT THAT STATES A PROFIT-SHIFTING PARAMETER, and it is the module's own: a 0.8 semi-elasticity, i.e. Heckemeyer & Overesch. Options 2.0's Option 11 prices 21%->15% at +978.9 conventional / +847.7 dynamic - a per-point COST of 163.2 against a per-point YIELD of 126.6 in the same edition, which is the base-response asymmetry a linear identity cannot carry.

column15: Conventional. PWBM publishes no dollar revenue feedback for the line; the tax provisions as a group move debt -11.16%, GDP -0.49% and capital -1.52% by 2050 (Table 3). PWBM's note that a rate increase alone "would increase corporate investment in the near-term" under current depreciation - because it taxes rents - is the clearest published statement that the sign of the investment channel depends on what the rate change is stacked with.
